newsitem.title: USA: USDA approves North Dakota oilseed plant loan.
newsitem.headline: USDA approves North Dakota oilseed plant loan.

text.p: The U.S. Department of Agriculture approved a 10-year interest-free loan to help start a new oilseed processing plant here, sources familiar with the plant said Thursday.
The $400,000 loan would be one source of financial support for the proposed plant, which would be operated by AgGrow Oils, a limited liability company.
USDA will make the loan to Northern Plains Electric Cooperative, a rural electric utility, which, in turn, will lend the money to AgGrow Oils, a Northern Plains spokesman said.

AgGrow Oils said construction on the plant is due to start in April, and the company said it expects to hold its first oilseed crush in fall 1997. The plant will process specialty oils such as crambe for edible and industrial markets and should have a starting capacity of 200 tons per day.

A spokeswoman for AgGrow Oils said an initial equity drive that ended in January raised about $3.4 million from investors. The company is seeking another $3.6 million to finance the first phase of construction.
